model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between model accuracy (ACC, in percent) and the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹ to 10³. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, spans from 0 to 65 with major gridlines at 5% intervals. Six distinct methods are compared: Base (black line with circle markers), FT (blue line with triangle markers), IKE (red line with triangle markers), MEND (brown line with square markers), MEMIT (purple line with diamond markers), and ROME (green line with square markers). The ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, starting near 45% at 10¹ and remaining relatively stable around 40–45%. In contrast, the Base method shows a steady decline from approximately 38% at 10¹ to about 30% at 10³. FT and IKE exhibit similar downward trends, beginning near 35% and falling to roughly 30% and 28%, respectively. MEND and MEMIT start near 39% and 38%, respectively, at 10¹, then gradually decrease to about 33% and 31% at 10³. All lines show a general decline or plateau as co-occurrence number increases, with ROME being the only method maintaining relatively high performance.
